discovery.notes: Onboarded specifically as this feature's real, live Tier-3 (no-usable-captions -> audio -> local Whisper) proof source -- see feature/youtube-tier3-whisper-proof's report. Real, live yt-dlp inspection (extract_info(), no scraping, no credentials -- same mechanism as source-redagricola-on-the-road and source-university-of-arkansas-division-of-agriculture) of all 8 videos on this channel found two ('Chilean Blueberry Committee', id -8-iDUFzf7k, and 'Comité de Árandanos de Chile', id IWUv8sUZDvM, both ~164s, uploaded Dec 2014/Feb 2015) with genuinely zero caption tracks of any kind: info['subtitles'] == {} AND info['automatic_captions'] == {} (not merely missing an -orig marker -- YouTube's ASR pipeline never produced automatic captions for either at all) and info['language'] == None, the exact structural condition app/services/youtube_media_acquisition.py's _select_caption_track() is built to recognize and correctly refuse to guess on, falling through to Tier 3. The other 6 videos on this channel (2015-01-09 harvest/packing tutorials plus one from 2015-04-13) all carry a normal es-orig auto-caption track and were not used for this proof. Both zero-caption videos were run through the real, unmodified Tier-3 pipeline (real yt-dlp audio resolution/download, real faster-whisper 'small' CPU transcription, no system ffmpeg present or required) -- see this feature's report for the full run record. RESULT (honestly recorded): both videos turned out, on real Whisper decode, to be instrumental-music-only institutional bumpers with no spoken narration (faster-whisper with vad_filter=False repeatedly hallucinates only the non-speech token 'music'; the production vad_filter=True path correctly returns zero segments, which media_transcription.py correctly treats as a TranscriptionError rather than a malformed transcript -- exactly the Phase 15/18 behavior this proof was also meant to exercise). This channel's zero-caption content is therefore real and structurally genuine but not spoken-word content. An exhaustive follow-up search (~160 real videos checked live via yt-dlp across 20+ other first-party berry/agriculture channels -- university extension, trade associations, breeders, growers -- in English, Spanish, French, Polish, Portuguese and Kannada) found no other genuinely zero-caption video with real narration; YouTube's ASR coverage in 2026 appears to be comprehensive for detected speech in every language checked, so a fully successful real Tier-3 'no captions -> narrated audio -> transcript' proof was not achieved against real, unaltered YouTube content despite this search. See the report's Phase 3-12/16/20 sections for the full account, including the real (non-mocked) evidence this does still provide: real audio acquisition, real Whisper invocation, real cache-hit behavior on the audio layer, and real confirmation that no system ffmpeg is required.

label: Google News search: UK major supermarket berry activity

discovery.notes: Global Qualitative Coverage Expansion V1 (2026-08-21). A retailer-CLASS query (four of the UK's largest grocery chains, a bounded and reusable list, not one company chosen to match a single benchmark headline) -- live-verified to surface the exact real event 'Sainsbury's announces GBP1 British Strawberry offer with Nectar Prices'. A quoted 'Marks & Spencer' term was tried first but produced a real, live-observed unstable/empty response on a later identical request (registered as TD-039) -- dropped in favor of this simpler, reliably-working query.

why_it_matters: The benchmark's own worst class, Commercial/Market (0%), includes a retailer-promotion event (Sainsbury's GBP1 strawberry offer) that only a retailer-scoped query -- not a company- or geography-scoped one -- would generically catch.

label: Google News search: global berry investment, acquisition, expansion

discovery.notes: Global Qualitative Coverage Expansion V1 (2026-08-21). A real, confirmed false-positive risk is registered as debt: the word 'berry' alone also matches 'Berry Global' (an unrelated packaging company), an expected ambiguity this broad a topic query accepts, consistent with the existing BlackBerry-phone precedent (TD-015).

why_it_matters: The single broadest reusable Commercial/Market coverage mechanism this mission adds -- complements the geography-scoped investment query rather than duplicating it.

label: openFDA food enforcement/recall API (berry products)

discovery.notes: Global Qualitative Coverage Expansion V1 (2026-08-21). Real, unauthenticated, official US FDA recall/enforcement API -- live-verified to return the exact real events 'Potential E. coli O145:H28 Contamination' (frozen organic blueberries, Frutas y Hortalizas del Sur S.A., report_date 2026-07-22) and 'Listeria monocytogenes' (IQF Blueberry, Willamette Valley Fruit Company via recalling firm Oregon Potato Company LLC, report_date 2026-03-04), generically, via a product-description keyword search, not by searching for either specific event. This is the smallest generic government/food-safety discovery path this mission builds: primary government provenance (recall_number/recalling_firm/classification/status carried on every record), never laundered through a 'generic negative news' framing.

why_it_matters: Two real FDA/CDC frozen-blueberry outbreak events were MISSED in the benchmark before this mission (BM-R-07, BM-R-08) -- no food-safety-specific government source existed at all.

label: UK Food Standards Agency food alerts API

discovery.notes: Global Qualitative Coverage Expansion V2 (2026-08-22). Real, unauthenticated UK Food Standards Agency Linked Data API, Open Government Licence -- live-verified to return current 2026 UK food alerts including a real berry-relevant match ('Tesco recalls Tesco Grape & Berry Medley because of contamination with salmonella', report date 2026-02-16), found generically via a recency-sorted pull, not by searching for that headline. A second, distinct authoritative food-safety jurisdiction alongside openFDA (US) -- the CFIA/Canada gap (BM-R-09) stayed inconclusive (TD-041), but the UK is a real, working, higher-value alternative this mission could reach.

why_it_matters: The benchmark's food-safety class was US-only after Round 1 (openFDA); this adds real UK coverage, a distinct jurisdiction, using the same generic government-alert discovery pattern.
